The global scope contains `pkgbase`, `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `options`, `source`, `sha256sums`, and `noextract`, all literal arrays/strings with single-quoted values. There is no command substitution (`$(...)` or backticks), no `eval`, no `base64`/hex-encoded blob, no `curl`/`wget`, no redirection or file modification, and no `pkgver()` function that could be run.

Every `source` entry points at a GitHub release asset on the same repository declared in `url` (`https://github.com/rsd/omarchy-onnxruntime`), which is also the repo named in the header comment as the generator's origin — an internally consistent, expected upstream source for a `-bin` package that repackages prebuilt `onnxruntime-split` artifacts. Unlike the unpinned-VCS pattern, these are immutable tagged release URLs with concrete `sha256sums` for all six assets, so nothing is fetched or executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` regardless.

All `bsdtar` extraction, `mv` of license directories, and dependency metadata live inside the six `package_*()` functions, which this command does not invoke; they are out of scope for this gate and would be reviewed in the full audit. Nothing in the top-level scope exfiltrates data, downloads code, or touches the filesystem, so parsing this file is safe.
</details>
